title: Vegan TikTok Hacks Tested: Mugs Cakes, Samoas, Banana Ice Cream and More (Goodful)
summary: Goodful tests a curated set of popular vegan TikTok hacks, ranging from a quick Oreo mug cake to frozen-fruit-based desserts and simple no-bake cookies. The host narrates the preparation and then rates each result, revealing a spectrum of outcomes: the Oreo mug cake comes out fudgy and solid (8/10), sour patch grapes with lime juice land around 3/10, a milk substitute from almond butter and water lands at 5/10, and a frozen-blueberry “ice cream” approach rates around 6/10. The trio of 3-ingredient ideas includes a banana-coconut-chocolate dough described as “vegan smells” with cookies baked to 15–20 minutes and cooled; a Samoa-like cookie earns about 8/10. A banana-based blender ice cream hits a perfect 10/10, and date-peanut butter-chocolate bites score 9/10. The episode also covers a cookie-dough-based base using blended oats (flattening and baking attempts yield a 2/10), and ends with an ice-cream-sandwich hack that earns an 8/10. Across hacks, the video emphasizes ease of execution and taste, while noting texture and ingredient limits where relevant.

sections.title: Oreo mug cake (microwave)
sections.description: Crush 4 Oreos with a splash of almond milk, microwave the mixture for about a minute, and evaluate the fudgy, quick dessert texture and flavor, rating the result (host gives 8/10).

sections.title: Sour Patch grapes with lime juice
sections.description: Cut green grapes, squeeze lime juice over halves, and assess whether the salty-sweet, gummy-like texture approximates Sour Patch Kids (rating around 3/10).

sections.title: Almond milk from almond butter and water
sections.description: Blend one tablespoon almond butter with one cup water (no straining). Observe froth and bottom chunks, note taste comparable to almond milk but with floaties; rating around 5/10.

sections.title: Blueberry-based ice cream alternative
sections.description: Combine frozen blueberries with any milk, let sit, then stir and crush. Result resembles ice cream in texture but not true ice cream; rating around 6/10.

sections.title: Three-ingredient vegan smells (banana-coconut-chocolate)
sections.description: Mix 2 bananas with 2 cups shredded coconut and chocolate; form circular shapes; bake 15–20 minutes; cool and sample. Host expresses excitement and assigns a savory verdict (later tasting around 8/10 for the final product).

sections.title: Samoas-like cookies (three-ingredient base)
sections.description: Prepare a three-ingredient oat-based cookie dough; flatten into shapes; bake ~15 minutes; drizzle with melted chocolate; chill to harden. Tasting yields an 8/10 with caveats about flattening technique and potential texture differences from traditional Samoas.

sections.title: Oat-cookie dough base with toppings
sections.description: Combine two cups blended oats (to imitate flour), two tablespoons coconut sugar, add a splash of almond milk; mix in chocolate chips; attempt to flatten into cookies; bake 10–13 minutes, extended to 17 minutes due to texture; result deemed disappointing (2/10) though still edible.

sections.title: Ice cream sandwich hack with cookies
sections.description: Use cookies from the prior section to assemble an ice cream sandwich; functionally successful with an 8/10 rating; host notes the combination works best with vanilla ice cream and suggests freezing techniques for a better finish.
